controls.context: They power the dimming of the caution and warning lights, the instrument lights and the landing and taxi lamps.

controls.name: Engine and hydraulic circuit breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: R ENG AUX DOORS and R OIL & HYD IND FUEL QTY SEL.
controls.context: They power the right engine's aux intake doors and the right oil and hydraulic indicators with the fuel quantity selection.

controls.name: Pitot, oxygen and cabin air circuit breakers (3)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: PITOT HEATER, OXY QTY & CANOPY SEAL and CABIN AIR VALVES.
controls.context: They power the pitot heater, the oxygen quantity gauge with the canopy seal and the cabin air valves.

areas.name: Pedestal
areas.text: The pedestal between the pilot's knees holds the UHF radio panel, the TACAN panel, the navigation mode switch and the front circuit breaker panel.

panels.name: Pedestal (overview)
panels.text: The pedestal is the panel block between the pilot's knees under the instrument panel. It holds the radio, the TACAN navigation panel, the navigation mode switch and the front circuit breakers.
panels.context: The pilot sets the radio frequency and the TACAN channel here before and during the flight.

controls.name: UHF radio control panel
controls.text: This is the control panel of the UHF radio, which the pilot uses to talk to other aircraft and the tower. It is described in its own panel below.
controls.context: The microphone button is on the throttle.

controls.name: UHF antenna selector switch (COMM ANT)

positions.name: UPPER
positions.text: The upper UHF antenna in the vertical stabilizer is used.

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The upper or lower antenna is picked automatically.

positions.name: LOWER
positions.text: The lower antenna is used.

controls.text: This switch picks which antenna the UHF radio uses: the upper one on the tail fin, the lower one under the fuselage, or an automatic choice.
controls.context: In AUTO the radio chooses by itself. The pilot may switch to the lower antenna when the upper one is shadowed by the plane.

controls.name: TACAN control panel
controls.text: This is the control panel of the TACAN navigation system, which gives bearing and distance to a ground beacon. It is described in its own panel below.
controls.context: The beacon is chosen by its channel number.

controls.name: NAV MODE selector (DF / TACAN)

positions.name: DF
positions.text: The HSI pointer points to the UHF station tuned on the radio (direction finding).

positions.name: TACAN
positions.text: The HSI pointer points to the TACAN station.

controls.text: This switch decides what the bearing pointer on the compass dial (HSI) points to: a TACAN station or a radio station tuned on the UHF radio.
controls.context: For DF the UHF radio function switch must be at MAIN or BOTH.

controls.name: Rudder pedal adjust T-handle
controls.text: This T-shaped handle would move the rudder pedals closer or further away from the pilot.
controls.context: The manual says it is not used or simulated in the game, although it may be pulled.

controls.name: Circuit breaker panel (front)
controls.text: This is the panel with the circuit breaker switches of the weapons. It is described in its own panel below.
controls.context: The pilot rarely touches them in flight.

panels.name: UHF radio control panel (AN/ARC-164)
panels.text: This is the control panel of the UHF radio, the radio for talking to other aircraft and the tower. The pilot chooses the frequency, the volume and the mode here.
panels.context: The pilot can pick one of 20 stored channels, turn the knobs to set a frequency by hand, or use the emergency GUARD channel. The frequency range is 225.000 to 399.975 MHz.

controls.name: Preset channel indicator
controls.text: This small window shows which of the 20 stored channels is selected.
controls.context: It is only used in PRESET mode.

controls.name: Preset channel selector
controls.text: This knob picks one of the 20 stored (preset) radio channels.
controls.context: A channel works when the frequency mode switch is at PRESET.

controls.name: Frequency selector knobs (100 / 10 / 1 / 0.1 / 0.025 MHz)
controls.text: These five knobs set the radio frequency digit by digit: hundreds, tens and ones of MHz, then tenths and the last step of 0.025 MHz.
controls.context: They work when the frequency mode switch is at MANUAL. The same knobs are used to load a new frequency into a stored channel.

controls.name: Frequency mode selector

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The frequency comes from the frequency selector knobs.

positions.name: PRESET
positions.text: The frequency comes from the stored channel picked with the preset selector.

positions.name: GUARD
positions.text: The radio goes to the emergency frequency by itself.

controls.text: This switch chooses how the radio frequency is picked: with the knobs, from a stored channel, or the emergency channel.
controls.context: GUARD is the emergency frequency that is monitored by others.

controls.name: SQUELCH switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The background noise is cut out.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The squelch is off so that weak signals can be received.

controls.text: This switch cuts the hiss of the radio when nobody is talking.
controls.context: With the squelch off a very weak signal can be heard, but the hiss comes with it.

controls.name: UHF volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the sound of the radio louder or quieter.
controls.context: It is the volume knob of the radio.

controls.name: TONE button
controls.text: While this button is held, the radio sends a steady test tone on the chosen frequency.
controls.context: The manual gives the tone as 1020 cycles per second.

controls.name: Function selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The radio is off.

positions.name: MAIN
positions.text: The radio sends and receives on the selected channel.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: The radio sends and receives and also monitors the emergency channel.

positions.name: ADF
positions.text: Direction finding. Not functional on the F-5E.

controls.text: This knob turns the radio on and picks what it does. MAIN is sending and receiving. BOTH also listens to the emergency channel.
controls.context: The ADF position was used in older F-5 versions and does not work in the F-5E.

controls.name: Hinged access door (preset load)
controls.text: This small hinged door covers the yellow LOAD button. The pilot opens it to reach the button.
controls.context: The door keeps the button from being pressed by accident.

controls.name: Preset LOAD button
controls.text: Pressing this yellow button stores the set frequency into the chosen stored channel.
controls.context: The manual says: set the frequency by hand, pick the stored channel, then press the button.

panels.name: TACAN control panel (AN/ARC(N)-118)
panels.text: TACAN is a navigation radio that tells the pilot the direction and distance to a ground beacon or ship. This panel switches it on and picks the beacon by its channel number.
panels.context: The pilot dials the channel of the beacon of the home base, and the HSI pointer then shows the way to it. The NAV MODE switch must be at TACAN.

controls.name: Channel display window
controls.text: This window shows the TACAN channel that is selected.
controls.context: The channel is a two-digit number with an X or Y mode.

controls.name: TACAN volume control
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the beacon's identification sound (a Morse call sign) louder or quieter.
controls.context: The pilot listens to the call sign to be sure of the right beacon.

controls.name: TACAN function selector

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The TACAN is off.

positions.name: REC
positions.text: Receives the beacon and shows the bearing.

positions.name: T/R
positions.text: Transmits and receives; shows bearing and distance.

positions.name: A/A REC
positions.text: Air-to-air receive; shows bearing to a cooperating aircraft.

positions.name: A/A T/R
positions.text: Air-to-air transmit and receive; shows range, and bearing to a specially equipped aircraft.

controls.text: This knob turns the TACAN on and picks what it does: only receive, receive and transmit for distance, or the same with another aircraft.
controls.context: The game labels it the 'TACAN Mode Selector Switch'. Air-to-air modes give the distance to a similarly equipped plane out to 250 nautical miles when both use channels 63 apart.

controls.name: TACAN channel selector (tens)
controls.text: This knob sets the first digit (tens) of the TACAN channel. In the game the mouse wheel turns it.
controls.context: Together with the ones knob it forms the channel number.

controls.name: TACAN channel selector (ones) and X/Y
controls.text: This knob sets the second digit (ones) of the TACAN channel. A right mouse click switches between X and Y.
controls.context: The X or Y part picks one of two channels with the same number.

controls.name: TACAN test light
controls.text: This light blinks while the TACAN tests itself and stays on steadily if the test fails.
controls.context: It is lit during the TEST button's check.

controls.name: TACAN TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button runs a test of the TACAN data on the compass dial (HSI). Flags appear on the dial and the pointer swings through set positions.
controls.context: The manual describes the test steps: with the function selector at T/R and the course at 180, the pointer swings and the range shows 000.

panels.name: Front circuit breaker panel (weapons)
panels.text: This panel on the front of the pedestal holds the circuit breakers of the weapon systems. Each one gives or cuts the power for a part of the weapon system.
panels.context: They are normally all on. If one is off, the matching weapon station or function does not work.

controls.name: Weapon station power breakers (5)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: WPN PWR LEFT INBD, CENTER LINE, RIGHT INBD, LEFT OUTBD and RIGHT OUTBD.
controls.context: One for each pylon station under the wing and fuselage. A station without its breaker has no power for its release or jettison.

controls.name: Weapon arming, release and mode breakers (3)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: WPN ARMING, WPN RELEASE and WPN MODE SEL & AIM-9-INTLK.
controls.context: They power the arming, the release and the weapon mode selection with the AIM-9 interlock.

controls.name: Jettison circuit breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: JETTISON CONTROL and EMERGENCY ALL JETTISON.
controls.context: They power the select jettison system and the emergency all jettison button.

controls.name: AIM-9 control breakers (2)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The system has no power.

controls.text: These are circuit breaker switches. Each one cuts the power to one system when it is switched off, or when it pops out after too much current. They are: LEFT AIM-9 CONT and RIGHT AIM-9 CONT.
controls.context: They power the control of the left and right wingtip AIM-9 missile launchers.

areas.name: Canopy, seat and mirrors
areas.text: These controls are on or around the seat: the canopy handle, the seat height switch and the two mirrors on the canopy frame.

panels.name: Canopy handle, seat and mirrors
panels.text: These are the controls for getting in and out and for sitting right: the canopy handle, the seat height switch and the mirrors on the canopy frame.
panels.context: The pilot closes the canopy before start-up. The CANOPY caution light says if the canopy is not locked.

controls.name: Canopy handle (open / close)
controls.text: This handle opens and closes the canopy, the glass roof over the cockpit. It opens backward and upward.
controls.context: A yellow CANOPY caution light comes on if the canopy is not locked. The jettison handle on the right vertical panel throws the canopy off in an emergency.

controls.name: Seat adjust switch

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The seat moves up while the switch is held.

positions.name: NEUTRAL
positions.text: The seat stays where it is.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The seat moves down while the switch is held.

controls.text: This switch moves the pilot's seat up or down so the pilot sits at the right height. It rests in the middle.
controls.context: The right seat height lets the pilot see the sight and the instruments well.

controls.name: Canopy mirrors (left and right)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The mirror is in view.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The mirror is folded away.

controls.text: These two mirrors on the canopy frame show the sky behind the plane. Clicking toggles them between in view and folded away.
controls.context: A pilot who is chased by another plane can see it in the mirrors.

areas.name: Stick, throttles and pedals
areas.text: The stick is in the middle between the knees, the throttles are on the left console and the pedals are on the floor. The buttons on the stick and throttle grips are placed so the pilot never lets go.

panels.name: Control stick
panels.text: The control stick in the middle between the pilot's knees steers the plane up, down, left and right. The buttons on its grip let the pilot trim, shoot, steer the nosewheel and talk to the radar without letting go.
panels.context: The stick is the pilot's main tool in a fight. Its buttons are placed so that thumb and finger reach them while the hand stays on the stick.

controls.name: Control stick (pitch and roll)
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward points the nose down, pulling it back points the nose up. Moving it left or right rolls the plane to that side.
controls.context: Pitch moves the horizontal tail and roll moves the ailerons on the wings. Roll is used to turn the plane, pitch to change height.

controls.name: Pitch and aileron trim button
controls.text: This four-way button on top of the grip trims the plane. Trim moves the neutral point of the stick so the plane flies straight without being held.
controls.context: Pushing it forward gives nose-down trim, pulling back gives nose-up trim and left or right trims the wing down on that side. The pitch trim dial on the instrument panel shows the pitch setting.

controls.name: Bomb-rocket button
controls.text: This button on the left of the grip releases bombs, fires rockets, launches missiles and dispenses flares, depending on what the switches on the left vertical panel select.
controls.context: If both wingtip missiles are selected, the left one goes first and the second press launches the right one.

controls.name: Pitch damper cutoff switch
controls.text: Holding this lever on the grip switches off the pitch damper, the helper that smooths nose-up and nose-down wobbles.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to take over quickly. The damper switch on the left console turns it on again.

controls.name: Nosewheel steering button
controls.text: While this button is held on the ground, the rudder pedals steer the front wheel, like a car's steering. Without the button the wheel is left free.
controls.context: In flight the manual says the button works as a second microphone button.

controls.name: Trigger (two stages)
controls.text: The trigger has two stages. The first stage opens the doors that let the gun gas out. The second stage fires the guns and runs the camera.
controls.context: The manual says that if the trigger goes straight to the second stage, firing starts after about 0.25 seconds because the doors open first.

controls.name: Dogfight / resume search switch
controls.text: This small switch on the grip works for the radar and the sight. Pushing forward picks the dogfight missile mode (DM). Pushing back picks the dogfight guns mode (DG). Pressing in cancels these.
controls.context: These modes make the radar look straight ahead at once and lock the first target found. The press in the middle also breaks a lock and restarts the search.

panels.name: Throttles and throttle grip
panels.text: The two throttle levers on the left console give engine power. On the grip of the right throttle are the buttons for the flaps, speed brake, microphone, sight, missile seeker and the chaff and flares.
panels.context: The pilot can set power and press these buttons without taking the hand from the throttles.

controls.name: Right throttle
controls.text: Moving this lever forward gives the right engine more power and moving it back gives less. Past IDLE the lever starts the engine, back to OFF stops it.
controls.context: OFF, IDLE, MIL and MAX are the marked positions. Past MIL the afterburner is lit.

controls.name: Left throttle
controls.text: Moving this lever forward gives the left engine more power and moving it back gives less. Past IDLE the lever starts the engine, back to OFF stops it.
controls.context: The left engine is started first.

controls.name: MIL / afterburner range
controls.text: Pushing a throttle past the MIL mark lights the afterburner of that engine. The afterburner burns extra fuel at the back of the engine for much more push.
controls.context: The game can hold the throttles at MIL like a spring stop. The manual says a key is needed for it.

controls.name: Throttle part 'FNRG R'
controls.text: The game lists a part of the right throttle under the name 'FNRG R'. The manual does not describe this part.
controls.context: The right throttle lever is described in its own entry.

controls.name: Throttle part 'FNRG L'
controls.text: The game lists a part of the left throttle under the name 'FNRG L'. The manual does not describe this part.
controls.context: The left throttle lever is described in its own entry.

controls.name: Throttle part 'THROTTLE DOG'
controls.text: The game lists a part of the throttle under the name 'THROTTLE DOG'. The manual does not describe this part.
controls.context: It has no known function in the game.

controls.name: Throttle part 'PANUHF VOL'
controls.text: The game lists a throttle part under the name 'PANUHF VOL'. The manual describes the UHF volume only on the radio panel on the pedestal.
controls.context: The UHF volume knob of the radio panel is described in the UHF panel.

controls.name: Flap thumb switch

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The flaps are fully up (0/0). This gives the longest range.

positions.name: FXD
positions.text: Fixed. The flaps are set by the air data computer according to speed and altitude.

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The flaps move automatically, depending on the angle of attack and the air data computer.

controls.text: This three-position switch under the pilot's thumb sets the flaps. Flaps are the parts of the wing that slide out for more lift at low speed.
controls.context: The flap lever on the left console must be at THUMB SW for the switch to work. In AUTO the flaps move by themselves with the angle of attack and the speed.

controls.name: Speed brake switch

positions.name: OUT
positions.text: The speed brakes open.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The speed brakes stay where they are.

positions.name: IN
positions.text: The speed brakes close.

controls.text: This three-position switch opens and closes the speed brakes, the panels in front of the main wheels that open into the wind to slow the plane.
controls.context: The brakes extend up to 45 degrees. They are moved by hydraulic power.

controls.name: Microphone button
controls.text: While this button is held, the pilot talks on the UHF radio. It works like the push-to-talk button of a walkie-talkie.
controls.context: The game also opens the radio menu with it. The nosewheel steering button works as a second microphone button in flight.

controls.name: Sight cage button
controls.text: While this button is held, the aiming mark of the sight is moved to the plane's fixed aiming line (cage). When it is released the mark returns.
controls.context: In the gun and dogfight modes the radar antenna is also lined up with the aiming line while the button is held.

controls.name: Missile uncage switch
controls.text: Holding this switch frees the seeker head of the AIM-9 missile so that it can look at the target. It springs back when released.
controls.context: A caged seeker looks straight ahead. An uncaged one follows a hot target, which the pilot hears as the missile tone.

controls.name: Flare/chaff release button
controls.text: Pressing this button throws out chaff and flares, as set on the countermeasures panel.
controls.context: The modes and the cartridges are set before the flight. Chaff confuses radar and flares confuse heat-seeking missiles.

panels.name: Rudder pedals and brakes
panels.text: The two pedals on the floor steer the rudder, the tail flap that turns the nose left and right. The top of each pedal also works the brake of the wheel on that side.
panels.context: On the ground the pedals steer the front wheel too when the nosewheel steering button is held. The brakes use the utility hydraulic system.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: Pushing the left pedal turns the nose left and pushing the right pedal turns it right. The rudder can move 30 degrees to each side.
controls.context: With the nosewheel steering button held on the ground, the pedals steer the front wheel.

controls.name: Left toe brake
controls.text: Pressing the top of the left pedal brakes the left main wheel.
controls.context: Braking only one side helps to turn tightly on the ground. Each main wheel has hydraulic multiple-disk brakes.

controls.name: Right toe brake
controls.text: Pressing the top of the right pedal brakes the right main wheel.
controls.context: If the utility hydraulic system fails, the brake valve still works by the pressure of the pilot's foot.
